dump.name: gtfo-inspection/dumper/dump.cs
dump.note: Local read-only copy. dump.cs records the declaring type, the il2cpp RVA, the vtable Slot of every virtual/override and the exact parameter list.

interop.note: The generated interop assemblies are Il2CppInterop runtime-invoke thunks: every body is `il2cpp_runtime_invoke(il2cpp_object_get_virtual_method(this, methodInfo), ...)`, so they carry the member set (type, virtual/override, Slot, parameter list, field offsets) but no game logic. Every call relationship below therefore comes from the native image, not from the interop bodies. The interop was used to confirm the two synced families exist and override Fire on their own type.

method: Read-only static analysis. No assembly is loaded into the CLR, no game process is started, nothing is written to a profile or to the game directory.

A method body starts at its dump.cs RVA, is bounded by the next distinct RVA of the same declaring type (the slot il2cpp allocated to it) and stops at the first terminator followed by int3/nop padding. Every method of the image is decoded, so an incoming edge is the complete set of literal callers of an RVA.
An edge is a literal E8/E9 rel32 call or jump at that site; indirect dispatch (vtable, delegate, register) is never reported as an edge.

Each of the four Fire bodies was additionally swept linearly over its whole own range, so a call placed after an early return or a tail call is still seen: that is the negative evidence that no Fire body reaches another.

An il2cpp virtual call loads the method pointer from the class vtable at `klass + 0x130 + slot*16` (VirtualInvokeData is 16 bytes) and calls the register. The base offset was confirmed on three known slots: `BulletWeaponSynced.Setup` reaches `CalcFireDelay` (Slot 150, 0xA90), `BulletWeaponSynced.UpdateRegular` reaches `Fire` (Slot 151, 0xAA0) and `PlayerInventorySynced.GetSync` reaches `OnSyncFire` (Slot 128, 0x930).

answer.question: Which Slot 151 Fire body runs for the local player, for a remote player and for a sentry; does any Fire body reach another; and does a client's shot reach a Fire body on the host?
conclusion: Slot 151 has exactly four bodies in this build and all four are distinct RVAs with rvaSharing 1: BulletWeapon.Fire (0x145FB30), BulletWeaponSynced.Fire (0x145D430), Shotgun.Fire (0x13C3020) and ShotgunSynced.Fire (0x13C2580). RifleWeapon and RifleWeaponSynced declare no Fire of their own and use their family's body.

No Fire body reaches another one. A full-range linear sweep of each body found no branch to any of the other three RVAs, so one patch per body publishes exactly one fact per shot and no shot can be counted twice; there is nothing to deduplicate against and nothing to inherit.

The unsynced bodies are the firing player's own. Both call PlayerSync.RegisterFiredBullets (BulletWeapon.Fire at 0x1460991, Shotgun.Fire at 0x13C3D44), which is the sending half of the shot replication, and both read FirstPersonItemHolder.

The synced bodies are this machine's copy of somebody else's weapon. They call PlayerAgent.get_Owner and SNet_Player.get_IsBot, they run BulletWeaponSynced.WhizByTest (the bullet-passing-near-you test) and BulletWeapon.TriggerSingleFireAudio, and they never register a fired bullet. Both synced classes also override IsFirstPerson (Slot 101) with a shared `xor al,al; ret` body (RVA 0x380300, shared by 297 method entries), while ItemEquippable.get_IsFirstPerson (0x13289C0) reads the instance's own byte at 0x170: a synced weapon is never first person.

A remote player's shot reaches the synced body through a static chain on the data side and a per-frame chain on the call side: PlayerSync.RegisterFiredBullets counts the shot, PlayerSync.IncomingLocomotion stores the replicated pPlayerLocomotion.FireCount (struct offset 0x15) into PlayerSync.FireCountSync (0x7C) and invokes FireCountCallBack, PlayerInventorySynced.GetSync reads that same field, passes it to the wielded item's OnSyncFire (Slot 128) and clears it, OnSyncFire forwards to its OnSyncCall delegate, OnSyncFireRegular/OnSyncFireBurst add it to m_shotsToFire (0x354), and the per-frame Update/UpdateRegular calls Slot 151 virtually once per banked shot.

The host therefore does run a Fire body for a client's shot: the client is a non-local player on the host, the host holds the client's weapon as a synced instance in a PlayerInventorySynced, and the count that instance replays is the one the client replicates about itself. The same is true on a client for the host's and the other clients' shots — the publication gate is what keeps only the host's copy from producing facts. What invokes GetSync itself is not resolved here and is listed under unverified.

A sentry runs no Fire body at all: BulletWeapon.BulletHit is static and its complete literal caller set is the four Fire bodies plus SentryGunInstance_Firing_Bullets.FireBullet (0x1414370) and SentryGunInstance_Firing_Bullets.UpdateFireShotgunSemi (0x1416B70). The sentry's own firing component holds its own static Weapon.WeaponHitData (s_weaponRayData, 0x8), so its rays arrive at the hit observer with no open shot.
consequences: The per-shot hook set is exactly the four Fire bodies: without the two synced bodies a client's trigger pull produces no fact on the host, and a host's trigger pull produces no fact on a client-side observer of that host.
The firing player of a synced shot is read from the weapon's own owner chain, so the shot fact names the player the weapon belongs to rather than the machine that observed it.
m_shotsToFire is consumed one unit per Fire call, so a burst or a delayed replay still yields one fact per shot rather than one fact per sync packet.

methods.name: Fire
methods.reason: The unsynced body. It is the one that tells the network about the shot, so it is the body the firing player's own weapon runs.

methods.name: Fire
methods.reason: The synced body. It reads the shooting player and the bot flag, plays the whiz-by and single-fire audio and never registers a fired bullet: it is the replay of a shot somebody else's machine already counted.

methods.name: Fire
methods.reason: The unsynced shotgun body: both hit call sites sit in the pellet loop and it registers the shot with PlayerSync like the rifle family does.

methods.name: Fire
methods.reason: The synced shotgun body: it declares its own copy of the spread logic instead of calling the synced rifle body, and it too never registers a fired bullet.

methods.name: RifleWeapon / RifleWeaponSynced
methods.signature: Gear.RifleWeapon and Gear.RifleWeaponSynced declare no Fire
methods.reason: RifleWeapon declares only its constructor and RifleWeaponSynced only PlayRecoilAnim (Slot 153, RVA 0x13C2420) and its constructor, so the rifle families use BulletWeapon.Fire and BulletWeaponSynced.Fire respectively.

methods.name: GetSync

calls.signature: virtual Slot 128 = Gear.ItemEquippable::OnSyncFire(System.Int32) on the wielded item, called with FireCountSync
writes PlayerSync.FireCountSync = 0 after the item consumed it

methods.reason: The only virtual caller of Slot 128 in the whole image: the synced shot count is applied to a non-local player's wielded weapon here and nowhere else. The count it passes is the one PlayerSync.IncomingLocomotion wrote from the replicated locomotion row. What invokes GetSync itself is not resolved (no literal caller, and Slot 18 is too common an offset for the dispatch scan to attribute).

methods.name: OnSyncFire

calls.signature: tail call to the DelegateOnSyncFire Invoke thunk with this.OnSyncCall (field 0x360) as `this`

methods.reason: The receive entry does nothing by itself: it forwards the count to whatever delegate Setup installed in OnSyncCall.

methods.name: OnSyncFireRegular
methods.reason: m_shotsToFire (0x354) += shots. It does not fire; it only banks the count.

methods.name: OnSyncFireBurst
methods.reason: Burst mode: m_shotsToFire += shots * m_burstMax (0x288). One banked entry per shot either way.

methods.name: Setup

calls.signature: delegate constructor for the Action stored in UpdateCall (field 0x368)

methods.reason: Both delegates are installed per instance: OnSyncCall dispatches a received count and UpdateCall is the per-frame consumer.

methods.name: Update
methods.reason: Every frame of every synced weapon invokes UpdateCall, which is the banked-shot consumer.

methods.name: UpdateRegular

calls.signature: virtual Slot 151 = Fire(System.Boolean) through klass+0xAA0, called with resetRecoilSimilarity = true

methods.reason: This is where a banked shot becomes a Fire body call: while m_shotsToFire is positive and the weapon's fire delay has elapsed, it calls Fire once and decrements the bank by one.

methods.name: IncomingLocomotion

calls.signature: writes PlayerSync.FireCountSync (0x7C) with pPlayerLocomotion.FireCount (struct offset 0x15, the 6th byte of the replicated locomotion row)
Action.Invoke on PlayerSync.FireCountCallBack (field 0xC8) when the count is non-zero

methods.reason: The replicated shot count arrives inside the locomotion row. Its only two callers are the spawn reconstruction and the bot locomotion path, so on the host this runs for a joining client (and for a bot).

methods.name: RegisterFiredBullets
methods.reason: The sending half. Only the two unsynced bodies call it, which is what separates the shooter's own weapon from the replay copies.

methods.name: BulletHit
methods.reason: Static and non-virtual, so this is the complete caller set. The four Fire bodies and the sentry's own firing component are the only things in the image that can turn a ray into a hit.

slotDispatchSites.note: Every site in the image that calls a virtual Slot through the class vtable, found by matching `mov reg,[reg+0x130+slot*16]` directly followed by `call reg`.

syncChain: The firing machine: a shot runs BulletWeapon.Fire or Shotgun.Fire, which calls PlayerSync.RegisterFiredBullets.
PlayerSync carries the count in FireCountSync (0x7C) and the low byte rides the replicated pPlayerLocomotion row (FireCount, struct offset 0x15).
Every other machine: PlayerSync.IncomingLocomotion writes the received byte into FireCountSync and invokes FireCountCallBack.

PlayerInventorySynced.GetSync — the inventory of every non-local player, including the client on the host — reads PlayerAgent.Sync.FireCountSync, calls the wielded item's OnSyncFire (Slot 128) with it and clears the field. (What calls GetSync is not resolved: it has no literal caller in the image and its Slot is too common an offset for the dispatch scan to attribute.)
BulletWeaponSynced.OnSyncFire forwards to OnSyncCall (OnSyncFireRegular or OnSyncFireBurst), which adds the count to m_shotsToFire (0x354).
The synced weapon's per-frame Update invokes UpdateCall (UpdateRegular), which calls Fire (Slot 151) once per banked shot as the fire delay allows and decrements the bank.
That call lands on BulletWeaponSynced.Fire or ShotgunSynced.Fire, which casts the ray, calls BulletHit and runs the whiz-by and audio for a shot by somebody else.

unverified.statement: That PlayerInventorySynced.GetSync runs on every machine for every non-local player, so the banked shot is consumed there.
unverified.reason: GetSync has no literal caller and its Slot (18) is a common vtable offset, so the dispatch scan cannot attribute it; the count it reads and the field it clears are proven, its caller is not.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace of OnSyncFire and Agent.Sync.FireCountSync while a remote player fires.

unverified.statement: That the chain above really runs in a live match, so one host shot and one client shot each produce exactly one synced Fire body call on the host.
unverified.reason: Nothing here was executed: the delegate targets Setup installs are runtime pointers this analysis cannot name, and the packet cadence is a runtime fact.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A host/client session with ForgeWeapon logging at info: one unmodified trigger pull per player and a count of the weapon.shot-fact lines, one per shot, attributed to the shooter's player reference.

unverified.statement: That pPlayerLocomotion.FireCount and PlayerSync.FireCountSync carry the number of shots since the previous sync rather than a running total.
unverified.reason: The receive path stores the packet byte into FireCountSync and GetSync clears the field after the item consumed it, and OnSyncFireRegular adds it to a bank, which is the shape of a delta; the sending side was not traced into the marshaller.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace of FireCountSync and m_shotsToFire across two consecutive shots.

unverified.statement: That a bot's shot also runs the synced body on the host.
unverified.reason: PlayerBotActionUseFirearm holds a BulletWeaponSynced and PlayerSync.SendLocomotion_Bot feeds IncomingLocomotion, both of which point at the synced path, but the bot's object graph was not walked.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime trace while a bot fires, or the same in-game log count with a bot in the team. Whether such a shot becomes a published fact still depends on the bot having a gtfo.player reference from its own domain.

unverified.statement: That the local player's own weapon is never one of the synced classes.
unverified.reason: The evidence is indirect: the synced classes report IsFirstPerson false, the two inventories are separate types, and only the unsynced bodies register fired bullets.
unverified.whatWouldSettleIt: A runtime dump of the wielded item's class for the local player and for a remote player.

limits: No claim about runtime behaviour: nothing here was executed, and a literal call edge only proves that a call site exists in the shipped binary.

The negative result (no Fire body reaches another) rests on a linear sweep of each body's own slot range; a body that il2cpp stored out of line from its type would be swept short, which can only under-report, never invent.

The vtable base offset 0x130 is inferred from three slots whose target is known from the dump (150, 151, 128); a slot whose target is reached through a different dispatch helper would not appear in slotDispatchSites.
An indirect call that loads its target through a register other than the one holding the vtable entry, or through a delegate, is not resolved.
